This guide documents the analysis behind **“Tech Dominates the Forbes Rich List. Do Tech and Finance Careers Really Pay More?”** Read the [blog article](https://xia071212.github.io/myrepo/blog/posts/post3/index.html), [README](https://github.com/xia071212/blog3repo#readme), and [analysis repository](https://github.com/xia071212/blog3repo). The article is generated as `blog_post.qmd`; its website source is maintained separately.

## 1. Source and sample

The source is [IPUMS CPS ASEC](https://cps.ipums.org/cps/), survey years 1976–2025. The extract contains 8,580,140 person records. `YEAR` is the survey year; `INCWAGE` and `OCC10LY` refer to the **prior calendar year**, so the final income series is 1975–2024. The source log in `results/source_log.csv` records the local file hashes and official source URLs. The microdata require an IPUMS account and are kept outside version control.

The analysis keeps ages 25–64, 50–52 weeks worked, 35–99 usual weekly hours, wage/salary class codes 20/22/24/25/27/28, identified civilian occupations, positive wages, and positive person weights. `HFLAG=0` identifies the original 5/8 questionnaire in 2014; a separate sensitivity uses `HFLAG=1`. Final main sample: **2,191,970 person-year records**.

## 2. Occupations and weights

The 2010-harmonized previous-year occupation defines four exclusive groups: Tech, Finance, Healthcare, and Other. Code definitions are in `code/occupation_codes.json`. Finance has 12 codes and an alternative seven-code sensitivity. The official historical crosswalk confirms that the rare 0400 occupation belongs in Other even though today's `OCC10LY` category list omits it. The corresponding crosswalk file is in `data/metadata/`.

Every population median uses the **ASEC person weight, `ASECWT`**. Within a group, sort incomes and select the first income for which cumulative weight reaches half of the group's total. The CSV already contains decimal weights; no further division by 10,000 is needed.

For monetary level comparisons across 2022–2024, convert each observation to 2024 dollars with:

```text
2024-dollar income = INCWAGE × CPI99[survey year] / CPI99[ASEC 2025]
```

The pooled age chart uses ASECWT/3. That makes the pooled weight total represent an average-year population; it does not change the median. The long-run premium uses a same-year ratio:

```text
premium = weighted median for Tech or Finance / weighted median for Other − 1
```

## 3. Outputs and interpretation

Figure 1 compares recent weighted earnings distributions in 2024 dollars: boxes span P25–P75, center lines mark medians, and whiskers span P10–P90. These are percentile whiskers rather than Tukey fences. All 60 plotted quantiles are independently verified against a weighted empirical CDF. Figure 2 compares age groups using three pooled income years. Figure 3 tracks Tech and Finance premiums relative to Other from 1975 to 2024. The supporting CSV files include unweighted sample counts and weighted population totals. The figures and numbers are generated by code, then inserted into the article; there is no manual result table in the article source.

The observed differences are descriptive. Age groups are different people, and income may come from more than one wage job during the year even though the occupation identifies the longest-held job. Coding changes, income disclosure treatment, and survey weights also limit historical comparison. This study does not estimate a causal return to selecting a career or an AI-specific wage premium.

## 4. Reproduce the analysis and figures

Replication means rebuilding the numerical results and statistical figures from the IPUMS microdata. Download the authorized extract and matching DDI to the paths specified in the [README](https://github.com/xia071212/blog3repo#readme), then run these commands from the `blog3repo` directory:

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 code/run_all.py
```

No website repository or Quarto installation is needed. The command saves the following outputs in `results/`:

| Analysis | Main outputs |
|---|---|
| Recent earnings and distributions, 2022–2024 | `recent_earnings_2022_2024.csv`, `recent_earnings_distribution_2022_2024.csv`, `figure1_recent_earnings.png` |
| Pooled age–earnings profiles | `pooled_age_2022_2024.csv`, `figure2_age_profiles.png` |
| Annual Tech and Finance premiums, 1975–2024 | `median_premiums.csv`, `figure3_long_run_premiums.png` |
| Sample construction and robustness | `sample_flow.csv`, `sensitivity_*.csv`, `quality_flags_and_topcodes.csv` |

SVG versions of all three figures and `three_figures.pdf` are also produced. The independent audit checks 1,844 estimate cells, 100 annual premiums, and 60 boxplot quantiles. It compares the 30 CSV columns with the matching DDI and checks duplicate person-year records. Review the verification reports under `results/audit/`.

`results/session_info.txt` records package versions, `results/source_log.csv` identifies the inputs, and `results/output_manifest.json` records SHA-256 hashes of analysis outputs. The script stops if a required check fails. Generating, rendering, or publishing the blog is a separate authoring task and is not required to reproduce these results.
